Translingual

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

kilo

  2. Alternative letter-case form of Kilo of the ICAO/NATO radiotelephony alphabet.

English

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • Hyphenation: ki‧lo

enPR: kē′lō, Rhymes: -iːləʊ

  • IPA(key): /ˈkiːləʊ/ (Received Pronunciation)
    • Audio (Southern England):(file)
  • IPA(key): /ˈkiloʊ/ (General American)

enPR: kĭ-lō′

  • IPA(key): /kɪˈloː/ (Indic)

Noun

[edit]

kilo (plural kilos)

  1. Clipping of kilogram.
    • 2013 July 26, Nick Miroff, “Mexico gets a taste for eating insects as chefs put bugs back on the menu”, in The Guardian Weekly‎[2], volume 189, number 7, archived from the original on 14 January 2025, page 32:
      The San Juan market is Mexico City's most famous deli of exotic meats, where an adventurous shopper can hunt down hard-to-find critters […] . But the priciest items in the market aren't the armadillo steaks or even the bluefin tuna. That would be the frozen chicatanas – giant winged ants – at around $500 a kilo.
  2. (international standards) Alternative letter-case form of Kilo from the NATO/ICAO Phonetic Alphabet.

Derived terms

[edit]
  • kiloware

Finnish

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈkilo/, [ˈk̟ilo̞]
  • Rhymes: -ilo
  • Syllabification(key): ki‧lo
  • Hyphenation(key): ki‧lo

Etymology 1

[edit]

    Borrowed from French kilo, likely through German Kilo and Swedish kilo.[1] By surface analysis, clipping of kilogramma.

    Noun

    kilo

    1. kilogram, kilo

      Hawaiian

      [edit]

      Etymology

      [edit]

      From Proto-Polynesian *tiro (compare with Samoan tilo, Māori tiro);[1] but disputed further.

      • According to Wolff (2010): from Proto-Oceanic *tidro (compare with Fijian tidro “to peer at something”) from Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *tindaw (compare with Malay tinjau “to inspect, to keep an eye on”).[2]
      • According to Osmond and Pawley (2016): from Proto-Oceanic *tirop (compare with Fijian tidro as above) from Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *tindap[3]

      Pronunciation

      [edit]
      • IPA(key): /ˈki.lo/, [ˈti.lo]

      Verb

      [edit]

      kilo

      1. (transitive) to watch, gaze

      Derived terms

      • kilokilo
      • mākilo
      • ʻōkilo

      Noun

      [edit]

      kilo

      1. watch or observer, someone who watches or observes

      [edit]

      3. ^ Ross, Malcolm D.; Pawley, Andrew; Osmond, Meredith (2016), The lexicon of Proto-Oceanic, volumes 5: People, body and mind, Canberra: Australian National University, →ISBN, pages 495-6
